Pros:
- Awesome art design, story, setting, and character design
- Building is a ton of fun and strategy is layered

Cons:

- Upgrade tree is very unbalanced. You'll feel 'equipped' for only the last 2-3 missions of the campaign

All the negative reviews are people whining about how they lost. This is a hard, unforgiving game, but that is what makes it so much fun. Here are a few beginner tips

1) You can pause the game to think about tricky situations. have some infected about to reach your houses? PAUSE THE GAME, locate all available soldiers, and start building a wall or spike traps in between the horde and your houses. (Note that if the infected are too close to something you can't build there)

2) You can press middle mouse button to make trees and mountains flat so they don't obstruct your view when you are building or looking if there is a gap in them. I saw a 200 hour review complaining about being unable to see gaps in trees. Ignore that.

3) For survival the number of infected and time until the final wave is customisable. start with the fewest infected and longest time to build up when learning the game. For the campaign, you can change the difficulty.

4) You will lose. Don't worry about it. when you lose a game you are a few hours into, don't rage, it happens to everyone. Think about what went wrong, and how you can do better next time.

I love this game. It was and remains a unique take on the RTS genre, and it has held up well. You're constantly engaged, making interesting decisions and balancing your economy. The emotional investment in your colony is real.

It's not without its deficiencies. Being able to watch replays of your game is sorely missing. For now if you want to relive it then Steam's video recording is the go. There's no multiplayer, and I'd really like to play it with friends sometimes. Groups of units can get stuck when walking through narrow gaps which can cause problems when you need them somewhere fast. The infected mutants are also unbalanced; their hearing is just too good. These are my biggest gripes. For what it is, it's near perfect. Kudos to the devs.

I hate that the hero missions are the ones with the biggest rewards, so you basically have to play them. But the hero missions are poorly designed and feature a ton of insta-kills from explosions that hit boxes are apparently bigger than the explosion animation. This would be fine if you could just save and reload, but the game does not allow for in mission saving, so you have to completely redo the entire boring, poorly designed mission. I wanted to play an RTS, but the game's mechanics basically force me to play a terrible RPG instead.
Missions are agonizingly slow and brutally difficult even at the lowest of difficulty settings. If you don't like yourself and want to waste your own time, sure... play this game.

This game is such a fresh twist on the Zombie Survival Genre. Building a town with an RTS game and surviving with towers and units. It is perfect for those who never got into RTS games before because of them being too competitive and having such a high learning curve. For those who don't have crazy high APM like Starcraft players you can pause the game and look around the map to make your decisions.

The game has a campaign coming, the survival and the custom maps alone are good enough reason to buy the game and it is a real challenge alone at the 100% score factor. The 800% score factor is insane, but doable once you get the hang of everything. Just watched a guy who did the 800% score factor without pausing.

Overall, the game is immensely fun and has a ton of replayability. I have never enjoyed an RTS more in my life.

If you love city-builders, strategy, and shouting at your screen while the last soldier dies next to an exploding farm—this is your game.

If not, run.
Gameplay is fun, but without a way to speed up the in-game time you end up staring at the screen for several minutes waiting for the final wave to arrive.

Be warned before you buy this game: this game has a permanent iron man mode, which can't be turned off in any way. What does this mean? That you can't save or reload your game. The game autosaves periodically or when you exit. This makes an already hard game even harder and playing it can often border on masochism. Beyond that, the game will throw zombies at you non-stop in such a way where you can't play it your way, there's the path of progression and building placement that's optimal, or you're screwed. Savor every moment of downtime you get because one tiny decision like where to move your limited amount of units during a zombie wave will screw you. The word for this game is insufferable. I want to like it, I want to recommend it, but it resists at nearly every step. At least the music and visuals are good. All this game needed for me to love it is to have a manual save function like EVERY. OTHER. RTS. But no, the devs wanted you to buy their game and suffer for it. It's too late for me to get my money back.

This game is very fun, but if you do not enjoy difficult games then this might not be the game for you. This is an RTS game where you build a base to withstand big waves of zombies that get larger over time, until the final wave where they come from every direction. The map is full of zombies as well that you must clear out throughout the game, unless you want the final wave to include all the zombies on the map. There are different maps that each generate different ways every time you play, but have the same general setup. The game has a lot of little things that make it difficult, but it's well worth taking the time to learn and play, as I have had a lot of fun with it.
As a side note, the campaign is not the most fun thing in this game, and I would recommend not stressing about playing it. The survival mode is the main reason to play the game.

I tried liking this game so much. I ignored the writing and worldbuilding that was apparently done by a nine year old, I turned off unit voices so I could ignore the cringy lines, I respeced the entire keyboard layout to fix the prehistoric keybindings - but the game's main flaw is and remains a childish understanding of difficulty.

It forces an iron man playstyle with no manual saves on missions that take hours, while making sure that letting even a single zombie through your defenses at any point in the game is an immediate game over. It announces waves that will assault your settlement at certain times, but then launches waves *between* those without warning or telling you.

There is no feature to speed up time. No manual save. There's missions where zombies are just slow-walking at you for fifteen minutes, even though the result is clear after one. Every time you fail a mission, you have to start over. Most missions are full of lengthy stretches of utter boredom, fulled by such insane difficulty spikes that they force you right back into starting the entire thing from scratch.

Ultimately, this is the first game of a great genre, and will hopefully remain its worst example.

I really really like this game, and am sad that there are no sequels or updates coming. If you want to play an RTS/Survival game that makes you sweat, it will be hard to find anything that compares to this IMO.

It's not a perfect game by any means, I think the controls feel a little hard to get into, especially for the hero missions, but if you get used to it they are very precise.

The campaign is really cool, especially on the first playthrough, I wish I could experience some of the missions again for the first time. There are some good custom maps and survival can be fun, so there is some long term playability, but realistically for most people I would say its more of a ~60 hour game like it says in the description.

So yea, if you like the Idea of RTS Survival games, give this a try, its real good. Just enjoy your time, cause there really isn't much else going on in this genre of games, and if you really like this you will probably be left wanting for more.
